reapack.desc: CuePort Sync — Artist comments as markers

metadata.description: {\rtf1\ansi\deflang1033 {\fonttbl{\f0\fswiss\fcharset0 Helvetica;}} \f0\fs22 \fs28\b CuePort Sync\b0\fs22\par \par Reaper integration for CuePort. The comments on a production, the artist's and the studio's, threads and all, are pulled into your project as native markers and drawn on a waveform inside the window. You can answer them from the DAW, delete a reply again, switch between every version the studio has uploaded, and send a new render back as a version without leaving Reaper.\par \par \b Features\b0\par - Device-code pairing with the CuePort studio portal, no passwords in the script\par - Production picker grouped by artist, with cover art and an inline search\par - Waveform of the active version with the comments pinned on it, click or drag to move the DAW cursor\par - Comment list beside it: the whole thread, artist and studio, replies indented\par - Amber for the artist, purple for the studio, on the pins and on the timestamps\par - Reply to a comment from the DAW, and delete a reply you sent\par - Project markers for the comments, optional, and a render start marker of your own\par - A/B compare against the uploaded version, routed past the master so the finished bounce stays uncolored\par - Render straight from Reaper and send it back as a new version, without the browser\par - The render settings are borrowed for the one pass and put back byte for byte afterwards\par - The finished render is shown to you first, with its length, its waveform and anything that looks off\par - Floating transport pill for one-click sync while the window is out of the way\par - Keeps itself up to date, through ReaPack when it manages this copy\par - Per-project binding, so every .rpp remembers its own production and version\par \par \b Requirements\b0\par - Reaper 6.68 or later\par - \b ReaImGui\b0 (install via ReaPack, required)\par - \b curl\b0 (bundled with Windows 10 and later, macOS and Linux)\par - \b SWS Extension\b0 (recommended, for reliable hover detection)\par - \b JS_ReaScriptAPI\b0 (recommended)\par \par \b Setup\b0\par 1. Install this package via ReaPack.\par 2. Open the Reaper Actions list and run \b cueport_sync.lua\b0 .\par 3. Click \b Connect to CuePort\b0 and approve in the browser.\par 4. Pick a production and bind it to the open .rpp.\par 5. Click \b Sync comments\b0 . Done.\par \par \b Time alignment\b0\par Comments are placed relative to the start of the rendered audio. Use the in-app Set render start button to align the ruler to your mix start.\par \par MIT licensed. The full text, the third-party notices and a list of everything the script touches in your project are on the About screen in the script itself.\par }

version.changelog:
CuePort Sync 1.35.0
Only one version is listed here, and it is the one that is really on the server. Older builds are not kept, so listing them would offer downloads that cannot be delivered.
FIXED
Two copies of Reaper running at once no longer fight over the script's temporary files. Those files used to carry a fixed name, so a request made in one Reaper could land in the other one's file. Each run now has its own.
Those files also moved out of the shared /tmp directory into Reaper's own resource path, next to the rest of your Reaper settings.
A cover download that was still running when Reaper quit used to leave its files behind. They are cleaned up now.
TIGHTENED
Everything the script hands to the command line is quoted, on both platforms: single quotes on macOS and Linux, double ones on Windows, where cmd.exe does not treat single ones as quoting at all. A resource path with a space or an unusual character in it now survives the trip intact. The pairing URL is checked before the browser is opened with it, and the page says so if it was refused.
The About page now says where your device token is kept: in Reaper's own settings, as plain text, the same place every script keeps its settings. A script has no way to reach the system keychain. It survives restarts on purpose, so you pair once and not every session. Log out removes it, and that is the thing to do on a machine you share or hand back.
WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES
Comments on a production, the artist's and the studio's, threads and all, are pulled into your project as native markers and drawn on a waveform inside the window. Pins and timestamps are colored by who wrote them. You can answer from the DAW and delete your own replies again.
Switch between everything the studio has uploaded: instrumental or mix, and every version of either. A/B the selected version against your own mix through a hidden reference track that plays past the master, so the comparison is fair. Cover art is shown in the picker and in the production header.
The script keeps itself up to date: a 200 byte check once a day, one button, and a restart into the new build. It works whether the copy was installed through ReaPack or by hand.
REQUIREMENTS
ReaImGui and curl. SWS and JS_ReaScriptAPI are optional and the Dependencies page says what each one adds.
